title: Auntie Lin's Scallion Pancakes
intro: Auntie Lin learned these running to a night-market griddle with Dad when they were kids, and she makes them so she never has to race for the crispy corner again. She rolls hers thin and flaky, while Grandma likes hers thick and chewy, so there are always two kinds on the table.

ingredients.name: flour
ingredients.feel: two big scoops from the bag, a little over

ingredients.name: boiling water
ingredients.feel: straight from the kettle, about this much, then a splash of cold if it's too dry

ingredients.name: scallion
ingredients.feel: a mountain of them, and when it looks like too much, one more handful

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.feel: a few spoons for the spread and more for the pan

ingredients.name: toasted sesame oil
ingredients.feel: one spoon, as much as smells good

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.feel: a good pinch, a little more than you think

steps.title: Make the hot-water dough
steps.instruction: Stir the boiling water into the flour with chopsticks until it looks shaggy, adding a splash of cold water if it is dry. Gather it into a ball and knead for a minute.
steps.sensory_cue: shaggy at first, then soft as a baby's cheek and bouncing back when you poke it
steps.quote: Boiling water goes in first. That's what makes it soft. Cold water makes it tough, like a shoe.

substeps.text: Stir the boiling water into the flour.
Add a splash of cold water if dry.
Gather it into a ball.
Knead for **a minute**.
Ready when **soft and bouncing back**.
substeps.detail: Ready when shaggy at first, then soft as a baby's cheek and bouncing back when you poke it.

steps.title: Cover and rest the dough
steps.instruction: Cover the dough with a damp towel and let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
steps.sensory_cue: the dough relaxes and a poke leaves a dent that slowly fills back in
steps.quote: Thirty minutes. Go drink some tea. The dough is working while you are not.

substeps.text: Cover the dough with a damp towel.
Let it rest for **30 minutes**.
Ready when **a poke leaves a dent**.
substeps.detail: Ready when the dough relaxes and a poke leaves a dent that slowly fills back in.

steps.title: Chop the scallions, mix the spread
steps.instruction: Chop a big pile of scallions into tiny rings. In a small bowl, stir the salt and sesame oil into a few spoons of neutral oil.
steps.sensory_cue: the scallions are tiny rings and the spread smells toasty
steps.quote: More scallion than you think. When you think it's too much, add one more handful.

substeps.text: Chop the scallions into tiny rings.
Stir salt and sesame oil into a few spoons of neutral oil.
Ready when **the spread smells toasty**.
substeps.detail: Ready when the scallions are tiny rings and the spread smells toasty.

steps.title: Roll thin, brush and sprinkle
steps.instruction: Divide the dough into four balls. Roll one into a very thin large circle, brush it all over with the oil spread, then cover it with scallions.
steps.sensory_cue: thin enough that you can see the shadow of your hand through it
steps.quote: Thin, thin, thinner. You should see the pattern on the counter through it.

substeps.text: Divide the dough into **four** balls.
Roll one into a very thin large circle.
Brush it all over with the oil spread.
Cover it with scallions.
Ready when **thin enough to see your hand’s shadow**.

steps.title: Roll into a rope, coil like a snail
steps.instruction: Roll the sheet up tightly into a long rope, coil the rope into a snail shape and tuck the end underneath. Press it flat with your palm to about a thumb's thickness and repeat with the others.
steps.sensory_cue: the coil feels springy, and no scallion is poking out of the edge
steps.quote: Snail shape. Tuck the tail under so it can't escape.

substeps.text: Roll the sheet up tightly into a long rope.
Coil the rope into a snail shape.
Tuck the end underneath.
Press it flat to **about a thumb's thickness**.
Ready when **the coil feels springy**.
substeps.detail: Ready when the coil feels springy, and no scallion is poking out of the edge.

steps.title: Pan-fry until golden
steps.instruction: Heat a thin film of oil in a flat pan over medium heat. Fry each pancake two to three minutes a side, pressing gently with a spatula, until deep gold and crisp at the edges.
steps.sensory_cue: the edges bubble and turn deep gold, the smell turns toasty and the sound is a steady crackle
steps.quote: Don't walk away. Medium heat, one pancake at a time, and listen. Crackle means crisp, hiss means too wet.

substeps.text: Heat a thin film of oil over **medium heat**.
Fry each pancake **two to three minutes** a side.
Press gently with a spatula.
Ready when **deep gold and crisp**.
substeps.detail: Ready when the edges bubble and turn deep gold, the smell turns toasty and the sound is a steady crackle.

steps.tip: Listen. Crackle means crisp, hiss means too wet.

steps.title: Scrunch, cut and serve
steps.instruction: Slide the pancake onto a board and push the edges toward the center with two spatulas to loosen the layers. Cut into wedges and serve while still hot.
steps.sensory_cue: you can hear the layers crackle as they separate, and steam comes out between them
steps.quote: Push it in, like this. Now you hear the layers cracking. That's how you know.

substeps.text: Slide the pancake onto a board.
Push the edges toward the center.
substeps.detail: Push the edges toward the center with two spatulas to loosen the layers.

substeps.text: Ready when **you hear the layers crackle**.
substeps.detail: Ready when you can hear the layers crackle as they separate, and steam comes out between them.

substeps.text: Cut into wedges and serve while still hot.

steps.tip: Scrunching loosens the layers so they separate and stay crispy.

stories.title: The crispy corner
stories.text: When we were kids, your dad and I would walk to the night market on Fridays with two coins each. There was a lady with a big flat griddle, and the crispy corner went to whoever got there first. Your dad always ran. I always lost. So I learned to make my own, and now the corners are mine.

stories.title: Thin or thick
stories.text: Your grandma says I roll mine too thin and too crispy. She likes hers thick and chewy. So at the table there are two kinds, hers and mine, and your dad always takes one of each and says he cannot choose.

special.text: Stirs toasted sesame oil and salt into the oil she brushes on
special.why: Most recipes brush on plain oil; the sesame oil and salt make every layer taste toasty and seasoned.

special.text: Pushes the hot pancake in from the edges before cutting
special.why: Most recipes just cut the pancake as it comes off the pan; scrunching loosens the layers so they separate and stay crispy.
